text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German debt slipped into loss in afternoon trading, still rivetted by any hints on the future of Europe's planned monetary union. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.79 down 0.10 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts ended 3/32 higher but off the session's highs as the market remained cautious amid renewed fears of a delayed single currency, analysts said. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-19/32, up 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - 10-year French bond futures settled higher but off best levels as profit-taking eroded gains. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.62 up 0.14 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt instruments closed around the day's highs, despite weaker German Bunds, as the market began to see signs of optimism over an EMU stability pact. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.85 up 0.97 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were higher in morning trade. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-20/32, up 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended sharply higher in Tokyo, propelled upwards by the yen's surge against the dollar and a drop in interest rate swap (IRS) rates, traders said. In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 123.88, up 0.59 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The highlight of the Eurobond session was Italy's 5.0 billion French franc 10-year bond, its first transaction in that currency. The deal, priced to yield 18 basis points over OATs, quickly sold out and was hailed a success by market players. "The bond was a big success," an official at joint lead manager CDC Marches said.

"We sold out of the bonds, and placed it with a wide range of investors, including many outside France. European investors have not been strong buyers of Franc bonds recently, but were attracted by the quality of the deal and its rarity," he said.
